name: Amazon MemoryDB
tagline: A durable, Valkey/Redis-compatible in-memory database on AWS backed by a multi-AZ transaction log.
description: MemoryDB looks like Redis or Valkey to clients but commits every write to a distributed, multi-AZ transaction log before acknowledging it, so it can serve as a primary database rather than a cache. Reads stay in-memory and fast, while writes pay a few milliseconds for durability. It adds vector search with HNSW indexes, data tiering to SSD on r6gd nodes, and MemoryDB Multi-Region for active-active replication with automatic conflict resolution. It fits microservice state, leaderboards or session data you cannot lose, on AWS.

pricing.notes: Node-hour plus per-GB write (data written to the transaction log) and snapshot storage charges; Valkey engine priced below Redis OSS.

scale.notes: Up to 500 shards per cluster; Multi-Region (Valkey 7.3+) replicates asynchronously across up to five regions.

strengths: Acknowledged writes survive node and AZ failures thanks to the transaction log
Microsecond reads with the full Redis/Valkey data-structure API
Strongly consistent reads from the primary
Built-in vector search for RAG and similarity lookups
weaknesses: Write latency is single-digit milliseconds, higher than ElastiCache
More expensive than a cache for the same memory
AWS-only; feature exclusions with Multi-Region (no data tiering or vector search)
useCases: Primary database for microservices using Redis data structures
Real-time leaderboards that must not lose updates
Vector search close to application data
notIdealFor: Pure caching where losing data is fine (use ElastiCache)
Large datasets that do not fit in memory economically
